description: The City Resilience Framework is a planning framework that helps city leaders, planners and investors identify resilience priorities and coordinate action across departments against shocks and chronic stresses, including infrastructure deficits and climate change. The 2024 edition, CRF'24, updates the first framework published ten years earlier and extends its use from whole cities to neighbourhoods and precincts, including masterplans for new developments and urban regeneration, drawing on a decade of experience from Chief Resilience Officers in the Resilient Cities Network. It is published by Arup, originally with support from The Rockefeller Foundation. The framework is available as a free download after completing a form on the Arup website; no licence is named. Caveats: the framework's goals and indicators could not be read today because the document sits behind the download form, and the Resilient Cities Network page carries no framework content. It supports structured, multi-sector resilience assessment and adaptation planning for cities; a related record is the Deltares Climate Resilient City tool.
